mainTopic: Conversion of a minor: רב הונא's rule that a בית דין may convert a child, רב יוסף's right to protest at adulthood, and new משניות on the כתובה amounts of different women
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier list of word meanings: an איילונית is named after a ram, a male animal that cannot give birth. A new משנה then teaches that a גיורת, a שבויה, or a שפחה who became Jewish or free before age three gets a בתולה's full כתובה of two hundred. רב הונא rules that a בית דין may immerse a קטן for conversion, because conversion is a benefit for a child who has not yet tasted forbidden things. An attempt to prove this from the משנה is pushed away: the משנה may be about children converting together with their father. רב יוסף adds that a child convert can protest and cancel the conversion when he grows up. אביי challenges him from the משנה's כתובה, and רבא challenges him from the קנס paid for these girls. Both challenges get the same answer: the money is paid only after she grows up, and her chance to protest lasts just one moment once she becomes an adult. The גמרא explains why each אמורא chose his own source, and then a new משנה begins listing which women get a כתובה of two hundred and which get one hundred.

steps.title: The word איילונית comes from 'ram'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its list of word explanations by saying that איילונית means 'ram-like', because she cannot have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: We too will say: an איילונית is like a ram, because she does not give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up an earlier discussion about where certain words come from by explaining the word איילונית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word איילונית sounds like איל, a ram. A ram is male and cannot give birth, so the name fits a woman who cannot have children. This is the last word explanation before a new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who cannot have children because her body did not develop normally
Male-like, ram-like (from the Aramaic word for 'male')
We too will say: introducing our own explanation of a word

steps.whatToRemember: איילונית is named after the איל (ram) because, like a male animal, she cannot give birth.

phrases.english: We too will say:
'Ailonit' means ram-like,
phrases.notes: The word sounds like איל, a ram, which is a male sheep.

phrases.english: because she does not give birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of word explanations from the end of the previous sugya.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: איילונית comes from איל: like a ram, she does not bear children.

steps.title: Women freed or converted before age three get a full virgin's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a convert, a captive, or a maidservant who became Jewish or free before three years and one day gets a כתובה of 200 and is subject to a virginity claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: A female convert, a captive woman, and a maidservant who were ransomed, converted, or freed when younger than three years and one day: their כתובה is two hundred, and a virginity claim applies to them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It teaches that these three kinds of women count as full בתולות if their change in status happened before age three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, women from these backgrounds are assumed not to be בתולות, so they get a smaller כתובה. But if the change happened before three years and one day, the משנה treats them as בתולות. They get the full 200, and the husband can make a טענת בתולים if he finds she was not a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who converted to Judaism
A woman who was taken captive
A maidservant (non-Jewish slave woman)
Marriage contract guaranteeing the wife money if the marriage ends
A husband's claim that his bride was not a בתולה

steps.confusionAlert: The three verbs match the three women in order: the captive was ransomed, the convert converted, the maidservant was freed. Not every woman did all three.
steps.whyThisMatters: Age three and one day is a key line in הלכה. Before that age, the body is treated as returning to the state of a בתולה.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The female convert, the captive woman, and the maidservant
who were ransomed, who converted, and who were freed,

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתוֹת מִבְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: when younger than three years and one day,
their marriage contract is two hundred.
And a virginity claim applies to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה; it has no connection to the word explanation before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גיורת, שבויה, or שפחה whose status changed before three years and one day gets a כתובה of 200 and is subject to טענת בתולים.

steps.title: A minor convert is immersed with the court's consent
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a קטן can be converted through טבילה with the consent of a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: a minor convert is immersed with the consent of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting רב הונא. He teaches that a child too young to decide for himself can still be converted, because the בית דין gives consent for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Converting normally needs the person's own agreement. A קטן is not old enough to give legal agreement. רב הונא says the בית דין stands in his place and agrees for him. This ties to the משנה, which talks about girls who converted before age three.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert who is a minor (a child)
They immerse (in a מקוה, as part of conversion)
With the consent and authority of the court

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for converting young children, and the rest of the sugya builds on it.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Huna said:
A convert who is a minor,
they immerse him
with the consent of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא גֵּר קָטָן מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by giving the rule that allows a young child to convert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן may be converted through טבילה on the authority and consent of the בית דין.

steps.title: Isn't רב הונא's rule already taught in a משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב הונא adds, since a משנה already teaches that you may benefit someone even when he is not present.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That conversion is a benefit for the child, and you may benefit a person even when he is not there? We already learned that: you may act for a person's benefit when he is not there, but you may not act against him when he is not there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. If his point is just that conversion helps the child, a משנה already says that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא guesses that רב הונא's reason is זכין לאדם שלא בפניו: you can do something good for someone without his agreement. But that rule is already written in a משנה, so why did רב הונא need to say it? The challenge pushes us to find a new point in רב הונא's words.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asking what is new here)
You may act for a person's benefit even when he is not present
You may not act against a person's interest (without him)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רב הונא is wrong. It only asks why he needed to say something a משנה already teaches.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That it is a benefit for him,
and one may act for a person's benefit when he is not present?
We already learned this:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in עירובין 81b.

phrases.english: One may act for a person's benefit when he is not present,
but one may not act against a person when he is not present!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's statement from the previous step, saying it seems to add nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a גר קטן is immersed על דעת בית דין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule rests only on זכין לאדם שלא בפניו, a משנה already states that principle, so רב הונא's statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Why רב הונא needed to say his ruling
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought a non-Jew prefers a life without rules, like a slave does, so conversion would not count as a benefit. רב הונא teaches that this applies only to an adult; for a קטן, conversion is a benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a non-Jew prefers a life without restrictions, just as we hold that a slave certainly prefers a life without restrictions. So רב הונא teaches us: that is only true of an adult, who has already tasted forbidden things. But for a child, conversion is a benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 4: why did רב הונא need to teach this if we already know you may benefit someone who is not present?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of benefiting someone who is not there only works if the act really is a benefit. We might have thought conversion is not a benefit for a non-Jew, because he loses his freedom from the rules, just as a slave would rather not be freed. רב הונא teaches that a child has never tasted forbidden things, so for him conversion is a clear benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken first thought)
A life without restrictions, free of the rules
So he teaches us
The taste of forbidden things
A benefit or privilege

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a בית דין may convert a child on its own: the conversion counts as a true benefit only because the child has not yet gotten used to a life without rules.

phrases.english: You might have said:
a non-Jew prefers a life without restrictions,
since we hold
that a slave certainly prefers a life without restrictions,
phrases.notes: A freed slave becomes fully Jewish and takes on more rules, so being freed is not seen as purely good for him.

phrases.english: so he teaches us:
that this applies only to an adult,
who has tasted the taste of forbidden things,
but for a minor, it is a benefit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by showing what רב הונא adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the ruling prevents a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Conversion is not a benefit for a non-Jew, because he prefers a life without rules, like a slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is only true of an adult who has tasted forbidden things; for a קטן, conversion is a benefit, so a בית דין can convert him.

steps.title: Trying to support רב הונא from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests our משנה supports רב הונא: it speaks of girls converted under age three, which seems to mean a בית דין immersed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say our משנה supports him: a convert, a captive, or a maidservant who were ransomed, converted, or freed when younger than three years and one day. Isn't this a case where they were immersed with the consent of a בית דין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring support for רב הונא from the משנה we saw in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl under three cannot decide to convert on her own. So if the משנה calls her a valid convert, it seems a בית דין immersed her on its own authority. That is exactly רב הונא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him
Is it not? (introduces the suggested reading)
They immersed them
With the consent of the בית דין

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
phrases.notes: This refers to our משנה from step 2.

phrases.english: the convert, the captive, and the maidservant
who were ransomed, converted, or freed,

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתוֹת מִבְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: when younger than three years and one day.
Is it not
a case where they immersed them with the consent of a court?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רב הונא's point, the גמרא looks for support for it in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a קטן can be converted with the consent of a בית דין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (step 2) about a convert girl younger than three years and one day.

steps.title: The משנה may be about children converting with their father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה may be speaking about a convert whose young children converted along with him, because children are happy with what their father does.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What case are we dealing with here? A convert whose sons and daughters converted together with him, since they are content with what their father does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 6 by giving a different case the משנה could be talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, the child's conversion may rest on the father's choice, not on a בית דין acting alone. So the משנה does not prove that a בית דין can convert a child who comes on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower reading)
A convert
They are content with it

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: a בית דין can convert a קטן because it is a benefit for a child who has not tasted forbidden things. The משנה does not prove this, because it may be about children converting with their father.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject רב הונא's ruling. It only says the משנה is not a proof for it.

phrases.english: No. What case are we dealing with here?
A convert whose sons and daughters converted with him,
since they are content with what their father does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רב הונא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the child was immersed by a בית דין alone. The משנה can be read as a case where the children converted together with their father.

steps.title: A child convert can protest when grown
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that children who were converted can protest once they grow up and cancel their conversion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: When they grow up, they can protest.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a new rule to רב הונא's teaching about converting a קטן. A child converted while young can refuse the conversion once he becomes an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said conversion counts as a benefit for a קטן, so a בית דין may convert him without his agreement. רב יוסף adds a limit: because the child never agreed himself, he gets a chance to reject it when he is old enough to decide.

keyTerms.meaning: They grew up (reached adulthood)
To protest, here meaning to reject the conversion

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is what the next two challenges attack, so it drives the rest of this section.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
When they grow up, they can protest.
phrases.notes: He means children who were converted while young. As adults they can say 'I don't want this' and the conversion is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב הונא's rule about converting a קטן by adding a right to protest at adulthood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child converted through a בית דין may reject the conversion upon reaching adulthood.

steps.title: Why give a full כתובה to someone who may leave?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף from the משנה that gives a girl converted under three a כתובה of two hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: A convert, a captive, or a maidservant who was ransomed, converted, or freed when she was younger than three years and one day gets a כתובה of two hundred. If you think they can protest when they grow up, would we give her a כתובה that she will take and use while living as a non-Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's rule with a question from our משנה. If the girl might cancel her conversion later, it makes no sense to pay her a כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats this girl as a full Jewish בתולה and gives her the full two hundred. If she could later reject her conversion, we would be handing Jewish money to someone who goes back to being a non-Jew. So the משנה seems to assume her conversion is final, against רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a wife receives if the marriage ends
Two hundred (זוז), the כתובה amount of a בתולה
Being a non-Jew
And if it enters your mind (if you really think)

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
A female convert, a captive woman, and a maidservant
who were ransomed, who converted, or who were freed,

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתוֹת מִבְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: when younger than three years and one day,
their marriage contract is two hundred.
And if it enters your mind that
when they grow up they can protest,
would we give her a marriage contract payment
that she will go and use up while a non-Jew?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that a child convert can protest at adulthood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה pays a full כתובה to a girl converted as a child; that only makes sense if her conversion cannot be undone.

steps.title: She is paid only after she grows up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כתובה is paid only once she has grown up and not protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she grows up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף. The משנה means she gets the כתובה only after she becomes an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was paying her while she could still back out. If payment waits until adulthood, the משנה no longer contradicts רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: When she grows up

phrases.english: Once she grows up.
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: she gets paid then, after she has grown up without protesting, not while she is still small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the timing of the משנה's payment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה pays her even while she is still a child who might later protest.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's payment happens only after she reaches adulthood.

steps.title: Even as an adult she could still leave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that even after she grows up, she could still protest and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when she grows up, she can protest and leave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Waiting until adulthood doesn't seem to help, because an adult can still protest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's rule gives the right to protest after growing up. So paying her as an adult seems just as risky as paying her as a child.

keyTerms.meaning: She protests
She goes out (leaves Judaism)

phrases.english: When she grows up, too,
she can protest and leave!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the כתובה is paid after she grows up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The right to protest begins at adulthood, so waiting until then does not remove the risk.

steps.title: The chance to protest lasts only one moment
steps.stepSummary: Once she has been an adult for even a moment without protesting, she can no longer protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once she has grown up for one moment and did not protest, she can no longer protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the protest right works. It is available only at the moment she becomes an adult; if she stays silent, her conversion becomes final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there is a short window, not an open-ended right. After that window passes, she is fully Jewish, and paying her כתובה carries no risk. The משנה fits רב יוסף after all.

keyTerms.meaning: One moment
She is no longer able

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף's right to protest is not a lifelong option. It exists only right when the child becomes an adult; silence at that moment makes the conversion permanent.

phrases.english: Once she has been grown up for one moment
and did not protest,
she can no longer protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגְדִּילָה שָׁעָה אַחַת וְלֹא מִיחֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11 and settles אביי's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the time limit of the right to protest.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An adult convert can protest at any time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The right to protest exists only at the first moment of adulthood; after that the conversion is final.

steps.title: Why give the fine to someone who may leave?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב יוסף from a משנה that gives a קנס to girls converted under age three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: These are the girls who have a fine: one who is with a ממזרת, a נתינה, a כותית, or a convert, captive, or maidservant who was ransomed, converted, or freed when younger than three years and one day. They have a fine. If you say they can protest when they grow up, would we give her a fine that she will take and use while living as a non-Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second, similar challenge, this time from the קנס (the fine paid for raping a young girl). The same girls converted under three receive it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנס is given to a Jewish girl who is a בתולה. If the convert could later reject her conversion, we would be paying her money she uses as a non-Jew. So this משנה also seems to treat the conversion as final.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed fine set by the תורה
Young girls (in the stage just after age twelve)
A girl born from a forbidden relationship
A girl descended from the גבעונים
A Samaritan girl

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
These are young girls who have a fine:
one who has relations with a mamzeret,
or with a netina, or with a Samaritan girl,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל הַגִּיּוֹרֶת וְעַל הַשְּׁבוּיָה וְעַל הַשִּׁפְחָה
phrases.english: or with a convert, a captive, or a maidservant
who were ransomed, converted, or freed

phrases.aramaic: פְּחוּתוֹת מִבְּנוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: when younger than three years and one day,
they have a fine.
And if you say that
when they grow up they can protest,
would we give her the fine
that she will go and use up while a non-Jew?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against רב יוסף, built the same way as אביי's.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule that a child convert can protest at adulthood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה awards a קנס to a girl converted as a child; that only makes sense if her conversion cannot be undone.

steps.title: The fine is paid only after she grows up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: the קנס is paid only after she grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she grows up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier answer, now for the קנס. She receives the fine only after she reaches adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the כתובה, delaying payment until adulthood removes the worry of paying a child who might later leave.

keyTerms.meaning: Once she grows up (the same answer as step 10, now applied to the קנס)

phrases.english: Once she grows up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא using the same reply given to אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the timing of the משנה's payment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קנס is paid even while she is a child who might later protest.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנס is paid only after she reaches adulthood.

steps.title: Even as an adult she could still leave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks that an adult could still protest and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when she grows up, she can protest and leave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its follow-up question for the קנס case. Waiting until adulthood doesn't seem to remove the risk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right to protest begins at adulthood, so the same problem seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: When she grows up, too,
she can protest and leave!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the קנס is paid after she grows up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The right to protest begins at adulthood, so delaying payment does not remove the risk.

steps.title: Silence for one moment makes the conversion final
steps.stepSummary: Once she is an adult for a moment without protesting, she can no longer protest, so the קנס is safe to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once she has grown up for one moment and did not protest, she can no longer protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same final answer as before. The window to protest closes right after she becomes an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות, the כתובה and the קנס, are explained the same way. The money is paid after adulthood, when the conversion is already locked in. רב יוסף's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: She protested
Once, since

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: a child convert may protest at adulthood. But the window is only the first moment of adulthood. If she stays silent, the conversion is final. That is why the משניות can give her a כתובה and a קנס, paid after she grows up.

phrases.english: Once she has been grown up for one moment
and did not protest,
she can no longer protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגְדִּילָה שָׁעָה אַחַת וְלֹא מִיחֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 and settles רבא's objection the same way as אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the time limit of the right to protest.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An adult convert can protest at any time, so paying her is risky.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the first moment of adulthood passes in silence, the conversion is final and the קנס may be paid.

steps.title: Why אביי did not use רבא's proof from the fine
steps.stepSummary: אביי avoided the קנס source because a קנס might be paid for a different reason: so that the sinner does not profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי did not challenge like רבא did, because there it is a fine. The reason for a fine is so that the sinner should not gain from his sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי did not bring the same challenge as רבא. אביי felt the קנס source could be answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is a penalty meant to punish the attacker. So חכמים might make him pay even if the girl may later reject her conversion, just so he does not walk away free. That means the קנס case does not prove much about her status as a Jewish woman.

keyTerms.meaning: a fine or penalty, here the fixed payment of a man who attacks a girl
a sinner who profits from his sin
there, meaning in the other source

phrases.english: Abaye did not say it like Rava:
phrases.notes: He means: אביי did not bring the same challenge to רב יוסף that רבא brought.

phrases.english: there, with a fine, this is the reason:
phrases.notes: "There" is the משנה רבא quoted, about a קנס for girls converted under age three.

phrases.english: so that the sinner should not profit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both challenges were answered, the גמרא looks back and explains why each אמורא picked his own source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only weakens רבא's source as a challenge. It does not deny that the קנס is paid.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קנס can be explained as a punishment for the sinner, not as proof that the girl is surely Jewish.

steps.title: Why רבא did not use אביי's proof from the marriage contract
steps.stepSummary: רבא avoided the כתובה source because a כתובה exists so that a husband will not divorce his wife easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא did not challenge like אביי did, because the reason for a כתובה is so that she should not be cheap in his eyes, which would let him send her away easily.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא did not bring אביי's challenge. רבא felt the כתובה source could also be answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כתובה protects a wife, so the husband will not divorce her lightly. As long as she has not rejected her conversion, she is a Jewish wife, and חכמים care for her. So giving her a כתובה does not prove that she can never reject the conversion.

keyTerms.meaning: the marriage contract, which promises the wife money if the marriage ends
light or unimportant in his eyes
to send her out, meaning to divorce her

steps.whatToRemember: Each source had its own possible answer. A קנס is meant to punish the sinner. A כתובה is meant to protect the wife from easy divorce. That is why אביי and רבא each chose a different source to challenge רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Rava did not say it like Abaye:
phrases.notes: אביי's challenge came from the כתובה given to girls converted under age three.

phrases.english: with a marriage contract, this is the reason:
so that she should not be light in his eyes to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This matches step 17, now from רבא's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only weakens אביי's source as a challenge. It does not deny that she gets a כתובה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A כתובה can be explained as protection for any current Jewish wife. It does not show that her conversion is final.

steps.title: New משנה: the כתובה of a woman whose virginity was affected in unusual ways
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says three unusual cases get a כתובה of מאתים. חכמים say a מוכת עץ gets only מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An adult man who was with a young girl, a young boy who was with an adult woman, and a woman injured by wood all get a כתובה of 200. These are the words of רבי מאיר. חכמים say: a woman injured by wood gets a כתובה of 100.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists unusual cases and asks whether the woman still gets a virgin's כתובה of מאתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first two cases, the relations do not count as taking away her virginity, so she keeps a virgin's כתובה. רבי מאיר says the same for a מוכת עץ. חכמים disagree only about the מוכת עץ: since her body is no longer intact, she gets only מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה
a woman whose virginity was ruptured by wood or another object, not by a man
two hundred זוז, the standard כתובה of a virgin
the Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An adult man who was with a minor girl
phrases.notes: Here "minor" means a girl under three, the same age discussed in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: and a minor boy who was with an adult woman
phrases.notes: Here "minor boy" means a boy under nine.

phrases.english: and a woman injured by wood:
their marriage contract is two hundred; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
a woman injured by wood, her marriage contract is one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier discussion has ended, and a new משנה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations of an adult man with a girl under three, or of a boy under nine with an adult woman, do not lower her כתובה. רבי מאיר says a מוכת עץ also gets מאתים, while חכמים say she gets מנה.

steps.title: A virgin widow, divorcee, or חלוצה from full marriage gets מנה
steps.stepSummary: A woman who is still a virgin but was widowed, divorced, or given חליצה after נישואין gets a כתובה of only מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A virgin who is a widow, a divorcee, or a חלוצה after full marriage: their כתובה is 100.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another list. These women are still virgins in body, but they get only a כתובה of מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These women already went through נישואין, the full stage of marriage, before being widowed, divorced, or released by חליצה. Even though they are still virgins in body, the משנה gives them only מנה. It does not give a reason here; the point is that a past נישואין lowers the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: one hundred זוז, the smaller כתובה amount (half of a בתולה's מאתים)
a widow
a widow released from יבום through the חליצה ceremony
full marriage, the second stage after אירוסין

steps.confusionAlert: "בתולה" here does not mean a girl who was never married. It describes each woman in the list: she really was married, but she is still a virgin in body.

phrases.english: A virgin who is a widow,
phrases.notes: "Virgin" goes with each woman in the list: a virgin widow, a virgin divorcee, a virgin חלוצה.

phrases.english: a divorcee, or a ḥalutza from full marriage:
their marriage contract is one hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתוּלָה אַלְמָנָה גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה מִן הַנִּישּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the next part of the same משנה. It now gives cases that get מנה even though the woman is still a virgin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A virgin widow, divorcee, or חלוצה whose status came after נישואין gets a כתובה of מנה.
